result:
Solution 1 is wrong because the set S contains more than just 3. Solutions 2 and 3 include girth values that I believe do not occur. This relies partly on a recalled result that I have not re-proved.

**Girth 3 occurs.** For G = V₄, the three subgroups of order 2 are pairwise adjacent, so Γ(V₄) is a triangle.

**Girth 4 occurs.** Take G = Z_{p²q²} with p, q distinct primes. The cycle p²–q²–p²q–pq²–p² has length 4, since each consecutive pair of subgroups has product equal to G. There is no triangle. Of the neighbours of the order-p² subgroup, the order-q² subgroup is adjacent only to p² and p²q. Those two are not adjacent to each other, because their product has order p²q. So the girth is exactly 4. This shows Solution 1's claim S = {3} is false.

**Girth 5 or 6 does not seem to occur.** I recall the classification (Akbari–Miraftab–Nikandish, on co-maximal subgroup graphs) as saying that if Γ*(G) contains a cycle, its girth is 3 or 4. I could not rebuild this from memory. I did check Z_{p³q²}, where the graph is K_{2,3} with girth 4, and that does not give 6. Solution 2's claim of 6 comes only from a hazy recollection and its own examples never reach it. Solution 3's claim of 5 has no support at all.

Under this classification S = {3, 4}, so the sum is 7. None of the three solutions (3, 13, 12) matches.

CHOICE: NONE
